channel.title: Kiran Goes Places - Blog
channel.description: Trip recaps, travel guides and honest write ups from Kiran Goes Places, to go alongside the videos.

item.title: Solo at My First F1 Race: The Japanese Grand Prix at Suzuka (Ft. Capsule Hotel)
item.description: I flew to Japan a week early with no ticket and no plan, then drove a tiny kei car across the country to watch my first ever F1 race at Suzuka. Here's how the Japanese Grand Prix actually went.

item.title: The 7 Best Places to See Mount Fuji from Lake Kawaguchiko, Japan
item.description: Not every viewpoint around Lake Kawaguchiko is worth the walk. Here are the seven that actually deliver, from a convenience store car park to a five hundred year old pagoda.

item.title: Everything Worth Eating in Tokyo, Japan as a Vegetarian
item.description: Tokyo has a reputation as a hard city for vegetarians. It isn't true anymore. Here's everywhere worth eating on a five day trip, from honey mustard gyoza to the best ramen of my life.

item.title: How to Spend 5 Days in Tokyo, Japan (First Time Itinerary)
item.description: Hidden bars in Shinjuku, flying sushi in Shibuya, sumo wrestling in Ryogoku, cherry blossoms in Asakusa and Mario Kart through the neon streets. Here's exactly how we spent five days in Tokyo.

item.title: 20 Best Things To Do in Tokyo, Japan (2026 Travel Guide)
item.description: Tokyo isn't one city, it's 23 different ones stitched together. From fighting a sumo wrestler to a whiskey bar the size of your living room, here are the 20 best things to do.

item.title: What I Wish I'd Known Before Hiking the Salkantay Trek, Peru
item.description: Altitude, weather, tickets, tour companies and everything else I wish I'd known before hiking the Salkantay Trek to Machu Picchu. The honest guide.

item.title: Cable Cars, Witches' Markets and Coca Leaves: Inside La Paz, Bolivia
item.description: South America's most underrated city. Cable cars instead of buses, dried llama fetuses at the Witches' Market, $10 fine dining and cycling Death Road. The full La Paz guide.

item.title: Five Days on the Salkantay Trek, Told Without Words, Peru
item.description: No talking, just the trail. Glacial lakes, a 4,630m pass, jungle glass domes and the walk into Machu Picchu, told entirely through the scenery.

item.title: The Machu Picchu Guide I Wish I'd Had Before Visiting, Peru
item.description: Tickets, circuits, mountain hikes, real costs and a genuine hack for when Circuit 2 sells out. The video I wish I'd had when planning my own trip to Machu Picchu.

item.title: Walking Into Machu Picchu Through the Sun Gate After 75km, Peru
item.description: Four days of the Salkantay Trek, a final brutal climb to the Sun Gate, and the moment Machu Picchu finally appears through the clouds. Is it worth the hype?

item.title: Three Days in Cusco, Peru's Underrated Inca Capital
item.description: Cusco is the gateway to Machu Picchu, but the city deserves far more attention than that. Three days exploring the city, the Sacred Valley and hiking Rainbow Mountain.

item.title: Four Brutal, Beautiful Days on the Salkantay Trek, Peru
item.description: Four days across glacial passes, turquoise lakes and dense cloud forest, climbing to 4,630m before descending towards Machu Picchu. The full Salkantay Trek, day by day.

item.title: The Night I Slept in a Hotel Built Entirely From Salt in Bolivia
item.description: Walls, floors, tables, beds, all carved from blocks of salt on the edge of the Uyuni Salt Flats. One of the strangest and most incredible nights of my life.

item.title: 15 Things Nobody Tells You About the Uyuni Salt Flats, Bolivia
item.description: Season, altitude, tours, photography tricks and why you need Wellington boots. Everything worth knowing before visiting the Uyuni Salt Flats in Bolivia.

item.title: Why I Set My Alarm for 5am to Watch the Uyuni Salt Flats Turn Into a Mirror, Bolivia
item.description: A 5am jeep ride onto a flooded salt desert, breakfast at a second salt hotel, and the sunrise that made our guide compare it to Bruce Almighty. Chasing the mirror effect on the Uyuni Salt Flats.

item.title: Flamingos, Geysers and a Train Graveyard: The Three-Day Drive From Atacama, Chile to Uyuni, Bolivia
item.description: A 4am border crossing, pink lagoons full of flamingos, bubbling geysers at 5,000m, llamas charging our group and an actual train cemetery. The three-day 4x4 road trip from Chile to the Uyuni Salt Flats.

item.title: We Almost Didn't See Rainbow Mountain, Peru, Because of the Clouds
item.description: A 3am bus from Cusco, altitude sickness at 4,900m, and a summit completely swallowed by cloud. What Rainbow Mountain in Peru is actually like, colours, crowds and the Red Valley bonus most people skip.

item.title: 4 Days, 4 Seasons: Hiking the Full W Trek Circuit in Patagonia
item.description: Granite towers at sunrise, a lake that never seems to end, the Cuernos up close, a windy final stretch to Paine Grande, and a walk on the Grey Glacier itself. The full 4-day W Trek in Torres del Paine, start to finish.

item.title: 10 Things I Wish I'd Known Before Booking the W Trek, Patagonia
item.description: Flights, buses, catamarans, and a campsite booking system split across two rival companies. Everything I had to figure out the hard way before hiking the W Trek in Torres del Paine.

item.title: The W Trek in Patagonia, Without a Single Word
item.description: No talking, just the trail. Granite towers at golden hour, a turquoise glacial lake, lenga forest, and a walk out onto the Grey Glacier itself, told entirely through the scenery.

item.title: The Day We Walked On Top Of and Inside a Glacier in Patagonia
item.description: A storm blew away tents overnight, then it was porridge, a hike along Lake Grey, and an ice hike onto the Grey Glacier itself, crevasses, an ice cave and all. The final day of the W Trek in Patagonia.

item.title: Four Seasons in One Day: Crossing the French Valley, Patagonia
item.description: A hanging glacier, an autumn forest that looks like a fairytale, two lookouts, and wind strong enough to whip a lake into tornadoes. Day 3 of the W Trek in Patagonia.

item.title: The Sunrise Most Hikers Skip, and the Longest Day of the W Trek, Patagonia
item.description: A 4:30am hike back up to Las Torres for sunrise, then 23km along a turquoise lake past Los Cuernos to Camping Frances. The longest day of the W Trek in Patagonia.

item.title: Forgetting Our Lunch and Still Making It to the Base of the Towers, Patagonia
item.description: A sleepy bus from Puerto Natales, a footbridge over glacial rapids, a fridge full of forgotten cheese sandwiches, and a cloudy first look at Las Torres. Day 1 of the W Trek in Patagonia.

item.title: The Colombia Itinerary I'd Actually Follow, Whether You've Got 2, 3 or 4 Weeks
item.description: Medellín's Comuna 13, the rock at Guatapé, birdwatching in Minca, a hammock over the sea in Tayrona, dancing in Cartagena, coffee in Salento and Bogotá's gold museum. Here's how I'd actually route a first trip to Colombia.

item.title: A Day in Bogotá, Colombia: Gold Masks, Bronze Nudes and a Guy Walking His Pet Llama
item.description: Most travellers skip Bogotá entirely or just pass through. Here's why one day in La Candelaria, the Botero Museum and the Gold Museum changed my mind about Colombia's grey, high altitude capital.

item.title: Eating Our Way Through Cartagena, Colombia: Coffee, Tacos and the Best Sushi I've Ever Had
item.description: Nia Bakery's V60 coffee, tacos in Getsemaní, a coconut lemonade in San Diego, and what might genuinely be the best sushi I've had anywhere. Everything we ate and drank across a few days in Cartagena.

item.title: Horses, Coffee and an Exploding Sport: The Best of Salento, Colombia
item.description: Galloping through a river on horseback, picking coffee cherries by hand, and a national sport played with gunpowder and beer. Seven things that make Salento one of the most memorable stops in Colombia.

item.title: Street Art, Statues and an Iguana in the Park: The Other Side of Cartagena, Colombia
item.description: Beyond the coffee and cocktails, Cartagena's old town hides a complicated history, some of the best street art in Colombia, and an actual iguana crawling through a city centre park.

item.title: Rain, Gunpowder and a Cloud That Finally Parted: Two Days in Salento, Colombia
item.description: Two days in Salento, Colombia, a misty Cocora Valley hike that nearly gave us nothing, a night of tejo with the locals, and a horse ride upstream through a river to a coffee farm.

item.title: Salsa Lessons, Bad Wine and a Very Iguana-Shaped Door Knocker: Three Days in Cartagena, Colombia
item.description: Three days in Cartagena, Colombia, a salsa class we booked to look less ridiculous on the dance floor, a painting-and-wine night by the pool, and what the door knockers of the old town actually mean.

item.title: Everything I Wish I'd Known Before Sleeping in a Hammock Over the Sea in Tayrona, Colombia
item.description: Two entrances that matter, a passport you actually need to carry, hammocks that creak all night, and a warning sign about currents that's worth taking seriously. Ten things to know before Tayrona National Park.

item.title: The Hostel That Feels Like Fiji, and a Night in a Hammock Above the Sea: Tayrona, Colombia
item.description: A boat-shaped grill, a DJ party we stumbled into by accident, a jungle offering to a big rock, and the strangest place we've ever slept. Two days in and around Tayrona National Park, Colombia.

item.title: Hummingbird Murals, Bulletproof Walls and 700 Steps Up a Rock: The Best of Medellín, Colombia
item.description: Comuna 13's murals and outdoor escalators, a michelada from a street stand, salsa lessons, Guatapé's giant rock, and the darker side of the city's history. The best things to do in Medellín, Colombia.

item.title: A Guide Named Richard Who Talks to Birds: 48 Hours in Minca, Colombia
item.description: A 5:45am wake up call for birdwatching, a waterfall hidden inside the forest, and a sunset viewpoint with a live band and torches. 48 hours in Minca, a mountain town tucked into Colombia's Sierra Nevada.

item.title: A 2-Hour Life Expectancy Joke and a Bachata Class: Three Days in Medellín, Colombia
item.description: A Comuna 13 guide's dark sense of humour, a wall of old newspaper front pages, and a spontaneous day trip to Guatapé with someone we'd met an hour earlier. A few extra days in Medellín, Colombia.

item.title: 7, 10 or 14 Days: How I'd Actually Plan a Guatemala Itinerary
item.description: Two days in Antigua, an overnight on an erupting volcano, and a lake with a 5pm boat curfew. How to structure a Guatemala trip depending on whether you've got a week, ten days or two weeks.

item.title: Erupting Volcanoes and a Bee That Bites Instead of Stings: The Best of Guatemala
item.description: Volcanoes, chocolate anthems, turquoise pools and a lake with five different personalities. Looking back at everything Guatemala threw at us, and where to find the full story on each stop.

item.title: My Weak Ankles vs an Active Volcano: What I Wish I'd Known Before Hiking Acatenango, Guatemala
item.description: Altitude sickness at 3,976 metres, a headlamp you genuinely can't hike without, and the shocker that some companies will carry your bag up for you. Ten things to know before hiking Acatenango, Guatemala.

item.title: A 9.5 Out of 10 Sunset and a Volcano That Wouldn't Erupt On Cue: Climbing Acatenango, Guatemala
item.description: Thrift-shopping for hiking gear, four and a half hours of volcanic sand, hot chocolate and marshmallows by a fire facing an active volcano, and a 5am sunrise hike to the rim. 24 hours on Acatenango, Guatemala.

item.title: Butts Up, a Coconut Halfway Up a Mountain, and the Prettiest Water in Guatemala: Semuc Champey, Guatemala
item.description: Standing on the back of a moving jeep, a slippery hike to the postcard viewpoint, and tubing down the Cahabón River while a guide shouts warnings about rocks. 24 hours in Semuc Champey and Lanquín, Guatemala.

item.title: The Sound They Used for Jurassic Park's Dinosaurs Was Real: 24 Hours in Tikal, Guatemala
item.description: A flooded island, a restaurant with a fireman's pole, a 4:20am wake up call, and a 2,000 year old Mayan city where 85% is still buried underground. 24 hours in Flores and Tikal, Guatemala.

item.title: One Lake, Five Completely Different Towns: Why Atitlán Isn't Just One Place, Guatemala
item.description: Sunrise hikes, hippy streets, a horse ride, cliff jumps and a hostel that feels like family. Why Lake Atitlán, Guatemala, is really a handful of different places sharing one volcano-ringed lake.

item.title: Free Beer, a Tent With Four Beds and a Scorpion Next Door: The Best Hostel We've Stayed At in Lake Atitlán, Guatemala
item.description: Free Cerveza on Lake Atitlán, family dinners with strangers who become friends, a hotly disputed cliff jump height in San Marcos, and a tiny scorpion in the tent next door.

item.title: Are You Really On a Lake If You Haven't Been Out On It: Top Things To Do in San Pedro & San Juan, Guatemala
item.description: The quick version of San Pedro and San Juan around Lake Atitlán, plus the one thing that's easy to forget about, actually getting out on the water.

item.title: A Solo Horse Ride, a 4am Sunrise Hike and Free Honey Until It Hurt: 48 Hours in San Pedro, Guatemala
item.description: A horseman who trusted me with his horse alone in the forest, a pitch black hike to Indian's Nose for sunrise, and a Mayan bee sanctuary where we tasted twelve honeys. 48 hours around Lake Atitlán, Guatemala.

item.title: Rumbles You Can Feel in Your Chest: Top Things To Do in Antigua, Guatemala
item.description: Green jade masks that once got buried with the dead, and a volcano hike where you camp opposite an erupting neighbour. The quick version of what to actually do in Antigua, Guatemala.

item.title: A Chocolate Anthem, a Coffee Farm Straight Out of Narcos and a Volcano at the End of Every Street: 48 Hours in Antigua, Guatemala
item.description: A chocolate making workshop that ended in a sing-along, a coffee farm that felt like a scene from Narcos, and the arch on every Guatemala postcard. 48 hours in Antigua, Guatemala.

item.title: The OG Lie Detector Test and Nepal's Best Kept Rooftop Secret: Top Things To Do in Kathmandu, Nepal
item.description: A fierce black statue that was once used as a lie detector, why Kathmandu's rooftops are its best kept secret, and the short list of what to actually do in the city before heading to the mountains.

item.title: A Very Nervous Haircut, a Monkey Stealing Coke and 24 Hours in Kathmandu, Nepal
item.description: A street barber who wouldn't leave my fringe alone, a monkey that stole a watermelon and then a Coke, and a city that's equal parts chaos and spirituality. 24 hours in Kathmandu, Nepal.
